findings.claim: New observation on 2cb3e0d1, outside the decision's literal condition. Line 78 tests control.fileFailed, control.failed and control.passed, which runVariant computes across every test file in the mutation include (../starter/src/**/*.test.jsx), not per file. A control run with one load-failing learner test file and one other learner file with a passing assertion therefore has passed === 1, skips the new branch and reaches the not-clean branch (line 82), printing the unchanged-copy message, exit 1. Observed on macOS (darwin), Node 24.2.0 and npm 11.3.0, in a 0700 scratch copy made with git archive of 2cb3e0d1 (2cb3e0d1a7057d24d12a8f87d1d16467a997b891), with the private overlay copied over the starter, npm ci in tests/ and TMPDIR pointed at a private scratch directory. Learner tests were the overlay's reference test and probes I derived from it in scratch, not independently written tests. Probe: the reference test plus a second learner test file holding the learner-side load-failing guard described under sme-fcc-x1. Normal run 'Tests 9 passed (9)'; the control report had numTotalTestSuites 2, numFailedTestSuites 1, numTotalTests 1, numPassedTests 1, with the extra file status failed and no assertion results; npm test printed only the unchanged-copy message and no marker string. With the 284d8903 verifier swapped into scratch the same probe got the same output, so it is not a regression, and it is learner-safe. It is inaccurate only in the multi-file case; README task 8 names one test file and allows splitting into more tests, not more files.
findings.recommendation: Accept as a recorded residual for v1; no correction loop needed. A later fix, if wanted, is to route to the unreadable message when any failed test file in the control report has no assertion results and no assertion failed, while keeping any real failed assertion on the unchanged-copy branch. Consolidate with edu-fcc-y1 and add the two-file case to the private adversarial controls.

Targeted by 2cb3e0d1 under Firstmate's decision (inbox 019): a load-failing learner test is an unreadable form and must receive the existing general safe unreadable message, without printing the suite error. The bound file changed in 2cb3e0d1 only by hoisting the general unreadable-form message into one constant (line 65), adding one branch after the no-runnable branch (line 78) that prints that constant when the control report has a failed test file and no passed and no failed assertions, and making the existing variant-run unshift (line 102) use the same constant. The message text is byte-identical to the one in 284d8903 (same 261 bytes). The no-runnable condition (line 74), every other message and the scoring of a clean control are unchanged. Observed on macOS (darwin), Node 24.2.0 and npm 11.3.0, in a 0700 scratch copy made with git archive of 2cb3e0d1 (2cb3e0d1a7057d24d12a8f87d1d16467a997b891), with the private overlay copied over the starter, npm ci in tests/ and TMPDIR pointed at a private scratch directory. Learner tests were the overlay's reference test and probes I derived from it in scratch, not independently written tests. Learner-side load failure: I added to the reference test a module-level guard that throws a distinctive marker string only when the imported default export's source text contains a string literal found only in the Task 8 variant wrapper, so the file loads in the normal run and fails to load under the check. Harness-side load failure: I appended a module-level throw with a second marker string to a scratch copy of tests/task8-variant.jsx and ran the reference test (restored afterwards; sha256 d85eae98... rechecked). Both passed the normal run ('Tests 8 passed (8)') and then npm test printed exactly one Task 8 line, equal byte for byte to the general unreadable-form message, and exited 1. Neither printed the unchanged-copy message, the no-runnable message, 'Vitest said' or either marker string, so the suite error is not exposed. Running the control variant directly for the learner-side probe gave exit 1 and a report with numTotalTestSuites 1, numFailedTestSuites 1, numTotalTests 0 and one test file with status failed and no assertion results, which is the case the new branch matches. With the 284d8903 verifier (sha256 6fe16b97...) swapped into scratch, both probes got the unchanged-copy message instead, so 2cb3e0d1 is what moves them. The reference test is still accepted with the Task 8 line and exit 0. A deleted learner file ('Test Files 7 passed (7)'), a todo-only file ('Tests 7 passed | 1 todo (8)') and a skip-only file ('Tests 7 passed | 1 skipped (8)') still get only the no-runnable message, exit 1. A single test that passes the normal run but has one real failed assertion against the unchanged control (its control report: one failed file whose one assertion has status failed) still gets only the unchanged-copy message, exit 1. A blank-only test gets the four completed-submission messages and a name-only objectContaining check gets only the team message, both exit 1. The outside-form aria-labelledby caption form still gets only the general unreadable-form message, exit 1. Technically, the new condition (a failed test file, no failed assertion, zero passed) sits between the no-runnable branch and the not-clean branch, so it can only catch control runs that produced no assertion verdict at all; any real failed assertion still reaches the unchanged-copy branch, and a clean control still reaches the variant scoring. Observed beyond the brief: a beforeAll hook that throws only under the check left its one test skipped in a failed file and also got the general unreadable-form message (it got the unchanged-copy message under 284d8903), which is within the decision's wording. One edge outside the decision's literal condition is raised as sme-fcc-y1. The claim is resolved.
